The Conquest of Sinope

Sinope, the jewel of the Black Sea coast, is held by the Greeks. Whoever holds it controls the trade between Anatolia and the northern lands. Sultan Kaykaus has resolved to take it, so that Seljuk caravans may reach the sea in the north as they already do at Attaleia in the south.
The Crimean Expedition

Kipchak raiders and Rus princes trouble the merchants of the Crimea, and Seljuk goods sold at Sinope must cross the sea to reach them. The Sultan orders an expedition across the Black Sea to seize the trading ports of the Crimea, as his armies did at Sudak.
A Storm in the East

Merchants and refugees pour in from Khwarazm with terrible news: a horde from the eastern steppes, led by a khan called Chinggis, is burning the great cities of Transoxiana. Scholars, craftsmen and whole families seek shelter in the lands of Rum.
The Sultan Falls Ill

Since the failed march on Aleppo, Sultan Kaykaus has been wasting away with consumption, and his physicians say he will not live to see many more seasons. The emirs whisper about who will follow him. If Kayqubad is to rule, name him heir in the family tree before the Sultan dies.
Kalon Oros Becomes Alaiye

The Greek lord of the coastal fortress of Kalon Oros has surrendered to Sultan Kayqubad, who has renamed it Alaiye after himself. A shipyard is being built beneath the cliffs, and the Sultanate now has a second window on the Mediterranean.
The Sultan of Scholars

Baha al-Din Walad, the great preacher called the Sultan of Scholars, has arrived in Konya with his family at the Sultan's invitation. His young son Jalal al-Din, who will one day be known as Rumi, already draws students of his own. Konya is becoming a city of learning.
The Sultan Han
On the road between Konya and Aksaray, the largest caravanserai in Anatolia has been completed. Its great carved portal welcomes caravans travelling from Tabriz to Attaleia.
Victory at Yassi Chemen
Near Erzincan, the armies of the Sultanate have routed Jalal ad-Din and his Khwarazmians. The spoils of his camp are rich, and the Sultan's soldiers return home as veterans.
Raise the walls
Stone by stone, the walls of the great cities rise again.
Summon the Turkmen
Riders from the frontier answer the Sultan's call.
The Sultan's Divan

The emirs gather before the Sultan. The horde has not yet reached Anatolia, but none doubt that it will. Some urge that the walls of Konya, Kayseri and Sivas be rebuilt in stone; others say the Turkmen of the frontier should be summoned and armed.
Grant the emirs iqta lands
The emirs receive rich estates and swear their oaths.
Rely on the ghulam guard
The Sultan surrounds himself with soldiers loyal to him alone.
The Death of Kaykaus

Sultan Kaykaus has died of consumption at the height of his power. His brother Kayqubad, whom Kaykaus long kept far from power, has been raised to the throne. The emirs who once backed Kaykaus watch the new Sultan closely. How will he secure the throne?
Build them
The great hans rise along the roads, and the caravans follow.
Leave it to the merchants
The merchants build their own inns and pay the Sultan for the privilege.
The Sultan's Hans
Trade along the Anatolian roads grows, but merchants fear bandits and harsh winters. The vizier proposes a chain of great caravanserais, a day's journey apart, built and guarded by the state.
Accept the alliance
Gifts are exchanged, and Khwarazmian officers visit the Sultan's camps.
Refuse and guard the east
The envoy leaves empty-handed, and the eastern garrisons are reinforced.
The Envoy of the Khwarazmshah

Jalal ad-Din, the last Khwarazmshah, has carved out a new realm in the east after fleeing the Mongols. His envoy proposes an alliance against the horde, but many at court fear the Khwarazmian more than the Mongols, for his armies plunder friend and foe alike.
Crush the revolt
The rebels gather in arms near Amasya. An army must march to break them.
Lower the taxes and pardon the tribes
The tribes lay down their arms, but the emirs and the treasury pay the price.
The Babai Revolt

Baba Ishak, a dervish preacher, has raised the Turkmen of the frontier in revolt against the Sultan's governors and taxes. His followers have taken Amasya and defeated the first armies sent against them.
Meet them in the field
The host of Rum rides out to face the horde.
Hold the fortresses
The Sultanate shuts its gates and waits for the storm to break.
Send tribute to the Khan
A heavy tribute is sent east, and the people are spared, for now.
The Road to Kose Dag

A Mongol army under the general Baiju has taken Erzurum and marches into the Sultanate. The Sultan has gathered his emirs, his ghulams and Frankish and Georgian mercenaries. History remembers what befell the Sultanate when it met the Mongols at Kose Dag; this time the choice is yours.
Alaeddin Keykubad

Seljuk Caravanserais
A chain of state caravanserais shelters merchants along the roads, and the Sultan repays the losses of those robbed on them.
Between Two Seas
With Sinope on the Black Sea and Attaleia on the Mediterranean, the goods of the north and the south cross Anatolia under Seljuk protection.
The Sultan's Guard
The Sultanate can raise as many ghulams and household troops as it can afford.
The Conquest of Sinope
Sinope has fallen and its harbour now serves the Sultanate. Merchants from the Crimea and the Pontic coast pay their dues to Seljuk officials.
Refugees from the East
Scholars, craftsmen and whole families fleeing the horde have found shelter in the lands of Rum.
Walls of the Sultanate
The walls of Konya, Kayseri and Sivas have been rebuilt in stone. The people sleep easier behind them.
Call of the Frontier
The Turkmen of the frontier have answered the Sultan's call, and their riders fill the ranks.
The Sultan's Illness
The Sultan lies ill in his palace, and the emirs are already choosing sides.
The Emirs' Iqta
The great emirs hold rich iqta estates from the new Sultan and have sworn their oaths to him.
The Sultan's Ghulams
Slave soldiers raised in the palace and loyal to the Sultan alone guard the throne.
Lord of the Black Sea
Seljuk governors sit in the trading ports of the Crimea, and the Black Sea trade flows through Sinope.
The Shipyard of Alaiye
From the shipyard beneath the cliffs of Alaiye, Seljuk ships sail to Cyprus, Egypt and Venice.
The Sultan's Hans
A chain of great caravanserais, a day's journey apart, shelters the caravans that cross Anatolia.
Alliance with the Khwarazmshah
Khwarazmian veterans who know the Mongol way of war share their hard-won lessons with Seljuk commanders.
Watch on the East
The eastern garrisons are reinforced and drilled against raiders from beyond the mountains.
The Sultan of Scholars
Preachers, poets and students gather in the madrasas of Konya around the family of Baha al-Din Walad.
The Sultan Han
The greatest caravanserai of Anatolia stands on the road between Konya and Aksaray.
Veterans of Yassi Chemen
The soldiers who broke the Khwarazmians return home as veterans, and the recruits want to be like them.
The Revolt Crushed
The rebels have been broken, but the Turkmen of the frontier will not soon forget it.
The Tribes Pardoned
Taxes on the frontier have been lowered and the tribes have returned to their pastures. The emirs whose lands were plundered resent the Sultan's leniency, and the treasury feels the loss.
The Host of Rum
Emirs, ghulams, Turkmen and Frankish and Georgian mercenaries stand together against the horde.
Behind the Walls
The Sultanate waits for the horde behind the stone walls of its cities.
Tribute to the Khan
A heavy tribute is sent east each year. The people grumble at the taxes but are glad to be spared.
